auxiliary_material: Description of the CD39/CD73 axis responsible for adenosine generation in the tumor microenvironment.
Details on T cell metabolic states (naïve, effector, memory, exhausted) and their vulnerability to adenosine.
Engineering strategies for localizing ADA1 on T cell surfaces (e.g., via CD26 or scFv).
Safety considerations regarding metabolic engineering, including risks of fueling tumor cells with inosine.
Statement that no clinical trials of ADA1/CAR T cells in humans have been conducted to date.
outline_action: ['Search for clinical metabolomics studies that profile purine metabolites (including inosine) in baseline tumor biopsies or blood from ICI-treated patients.', 'Look for microdialysis or mass spectrometry imaging studies quantifying inosine specifically in human tumor microenvironments.', 'Investigate literature linking gut microbiome-derived inosine to ICI efficacy, as the topic context involves microbiome-ICI interactions.', 'Prioritize studies that explicitly report statistical associations (e.g., hazard ratios, p-values) between metabolite levels and clinical endpoints.']
remaining_gap: ['No absolute concentration data for inosine (μM or ng/mL) in human tumor tissue or microdialysis fluid is provided.', 'No statistical correlation between endogenous inosine levels and ICI response (ORR/PFS/OS) in human patients is reported.', 'The efficacy data presented is primarily from preclinical CAR T cell models, not ICI monotherapy or combination trials in humans.', 'The review explicitly states that clinical validation for ADA1-based strategies is pending, implying a lack of human inosine-ICI outcome data in this source.']
useful_material: Mechanism description: ADA1 enzyme converts immunosuppressive adenosine to inosine, which can serve as an alternative carbon source for T cells.
General TME metabolite context: Extracellular adenosine concentrations in tumors can reach 100–200 μM, significantly higher than in healthy tissue.
Metabolic rationale: Inosine supplementation or generation supports T cell metabolism (glycolytic and pentose phosphate pathways) under glucose restriction.
Preclinical evidence: ADA1-expressing CAR T cells show reduced exhaustion and improved persistence in mouse models, linked to inosine availability.
Combination concept: The authors discuss potential integration of metabolic reprogramming (like ADA1) with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) as a future strategy.
